To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) satisfiability checking for equality logic with uninterpreted functions can be reduced to satisfiability checking for a logic of Boolean equality, (2) satisfiability checking can be performed efficiently for the latter by a combination of a Boolean satisfiability checker and a decision procedure for a theory of Boolean equality, and (3) the decision procedure can be based on a combination of BDD-based techniques, such as the BDD-based decision procedure for the theory of Boolean equality and the BDD-based satisfiability

(1) the satisfiability of the theory of equality with uninterpreted functions is NP-Complete and (2) BDD based procedures for satisfiability checking are superior to finite instantiation based procedures.

(a) BDD-based satisfiability procedures can be used to verify designs in the logic of equality with functions, and (b) the indicator-based satisfiability procedure is faster than the finite instantiation procedure for most designs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing efficient symbolic procedures for reasoning about equality with uninterpreted function symbols.
developing new procedures for satisfiability checking of the theory of equality with uninterpretted functions.
the design and implementation of a satisfiability procedure that is efficient and complete for the theory of equality with uninterpretted functions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the second procedure is the best one to use.
the second approach is better for most cases and the first approach is better in the rare case where the second approach fails.
the indicator variable approach is the better approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BDDs are not the right data structure for this logic.
the logic of equality with function symbols is not as hard to deal with as the theory of equality with unbounded integers.
the logic of equality with functions is amenable for BDD based procedures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the logic of equality with equality and uninterpreted functions is not as hard as the logic of equality without equality and uninterpreted predicates.
Boolean indicator variables for equality are an indispensable tool in satisfiability checking for equality with uninterpreted function symbols.
the theory of equality with uninterpretd functions can be efficiently checked by a combination of Boolean satisfiability checking and a theory solver for the theory of equality.
